title: Release notes + migration helper for Optimize Guardrails gating enforcement
author: Connor O'Brien
description: This PR adds a user-facing release notes entry and an operator-facing migration helper for the new Optimize Guardrails gating enforcement on “Optimize apply”. The goal is to make the behavior change explicit (and discoverable) before we move tenants from observe-only to soft-block/hard-block, and to reduce support load by giving customers and CSM/Solutions a concrete checklist for preflight readiness. Background: earlier PRs added enforcement plumbing (Optimize apply returns a gating decision with structured reasons), feature flags to stage enforcement, and safe-degrade behavior when the eval runner is unavailable. With stricter enforcement, tenants may see previously-successful applies become blocked due to failed quality thresholds, eval timeouts, missing prompt sets, or insufficient sample sizes. This PR documents what changes, what doesn’t, and what to do if you get blocked (rerun, add prompt coverage, adjust config delta, or request an audited override where permitted). It also adds a small migration helper that inventories tenants/routes impacted by the new defaults and prints actionable remediation steps (missing prompt set rev pinning, invalid/legacy Optimize config fields, no guardrail policy attached, or use of deprecated override flags). The helper is intended to be run by Redwood operators and (optionally) shared with enterprise customers running Private deployments. Scope: release notes entry + migration helper + a short internal operator guide. Non-goals: changing enforcement policy or thresholds (those remain controlled by GuardrailPolicy versions and feature flags), changing UI strings, or adding new audit log event fields.
commits: release-notes: add Optimize Guardrails gating announcement + FAQ
migrations: add optimize_guardrails_preflight script for tenant/route readiness
control-plane: add legacy config lints + actionable remediation messages
docs(internal): add runbook snippet for support/CS handling blocked applies
tests: add golden tests for preflight output and legacy config detection
notable_snippets: Preflight helper output (example): "tenant=acme-fintech route=/v1/chat/completions: BLOCKING RISK: missing GuardrailPolicy attachment (expected by flag optimize.guardrails.enforce>=soft_block); ACTION: attach policy version gp_2025_02_pilot_v3 or pin to gp_default_v1"

Release notes excerpt: "Optimize apply now runs mandatory quality evaluation checks for certain optimization types. If checks fail or time out, your change may be blocked depending on your enforcement tier. You can inspect gating results in Console and via API (gating_run_id, metrics, reasons)."

Legacy lint example: "Detected deprecated field optimize.allowUnsafeOverride=true; this will be ignored once hard-block is enabled. Use audited override pathway (requires RBAC) or request policy adjustment."
testing: Unit tests for legacy validation + guardrail policy resolver. Golden tests for migration helper output formatting. Manually ran preflight against staging snapshot and validated against 3 known pilot tenants (one missing prompt-set pin, one legacy override flag, one fully ready).
rollout_notes: No runtime behavior changes in this PR. This is purely documentation + tooling. Intended to land ahead of enforcement flag ramp (observe-only -> soft-block) so Support/CS can reference the release notes link and operators can proactively preflight the next batch of tenants. Preflight is safe to run read-only; it does not mutate policies or tenant configs.
release_notes: Optimize Guardrails: Quality gating for Optimize apply is rolling out in stages (observe-only -> soft-block -> hard-block).
If an apply is blocked, the response includes structured reasons and a gating_run_id. Inspect results in Console or via API.
Common remediation steps: add/expand prompt sets, rerun evals, reduce the config delta (e.g., smaller quantization step), or request an audited override where permitted by RBAC/policy.
Private deployments: operators can run the new preflight migration helper to identify routes likely to be impacted before enabling enforcement.
conversation: Aditya Rao (PM): Please make sure release notes clearly call out which optimization types are most likely to be blocked (quantization especially) and that the docs don’t imply we’re changing model outputs intentionally. Connor O'Brien (author): Updated the FAQ section to emphasize ‘guardrails prevent regressions’ and added a short list: quantization transitions are most sensitive; batching/caching generally lower risk but can still fail on formatting/tool-calling sentinel prompts. Ethan Park (Platform): Preflight helper should surface prompt-set rev pinning issues explicitly; we’ve had a few tenants with floating prompt sets causing confusing ‘same change, different result’ reports. Connor O'Brien: Added a lint that checks for promptSetRevision=null and prints ACTION: pin a revision or accept observe-only until pinned. Naomi Feldman (Security): Ensure the preflight output is safe to paste into tickets (no prompt content, no PII). Also call out audit log availability for customers asking for proof. Connor O'Brien: Output contains only tenant slug, route id, model id/version, and policy ids. No prompt text. Added a release note line pointing to OptimizeConfigChange audit events and included a Support playbook snippet referencing SUP-18544. Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please add a note on safe-degrade behavior; if eval runner is down, some tiers will block. Customers need to know it can fail ‘timeout’ vs ‘quality regression’. Connor O'Brien: Added ‘Timeouts / runner unavailable’ section and referenced the ‘retry later’ guidance + escalation path. Elliot Price (Docs): Tone is good; please align terminology with Console states (‘Passed’, ‘Failed’, ‘Timed out’, ‘Override requested’). Connor O'Brien: Updated wording and included the exact state names in the FAQ.
merge_summary: Merged ahead of enforcement ramp so operators/CS have release notes + preflight tool. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-3926 for the staged rollout communication plan and in PM-842 for customer-facing messaging consistency.
